structure.layout: Desktop app page under a dark top app bar. A page title row has a deadline pill on the right. Below it are two columns: a wide bordered panel holding the meter-reading sheet (filter tabs + search toolbar, an info strip, a scrolling table with editable reading inputs and a sticky keyboard-hint footer), and a narrow right sidebar with a progress card, a 'needs your review' queue and a 'lock the cycle' checklist. A thin footer sits at the bottom.

aesthetics.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for all UI text: headings, labels, names and buttons. Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with slashed zeros for meter IDs, every reading/usage number and the keyboard keys, so digits stay unambiguous when copied from paper.
aesthetics.typeScale: Restrained, legibility-first: H1 30px/700, big progress number 34px/700, readings 18px mono, body and table text 17px (above the usual 14-16), secondary text 14-15px, small uppercase letter-spaced section labels (NEEDS YOUR REVIEW, LOCK THE CYCLE). Weight changes between 400/600/700 carry hierarchy more than size does.

notes: Warm off-white 'paper' background (#f3f0e8) with white panels, thin beige borders, 9-12px radii and a deep teal header. It is aimed at older volunteer treasurers: large hyperlegible type, monospaced digits with slashed zeros, plain-language status ('Looks normal', 'Near zero, as expected', 'Not entered yet'). Each row is checked against the previous reading and the 12-month average. Flagged rows get a tinted background, a colored left edge and an outlined callout with 'Review'. Opening it expands an in-row panel that explains the numbers, offers 'one keystroke away' digit-transposition corrections and a meter-replaced path. Sidebar: route progress with readers' names, a 'Next to enter' jump button, a severity-colored review queue, and a dashed, disabled 'Lock cycle' button gated by two computed prerequisites shown as empty radio-like circles. A 'Saved on this computer' local-save indicator sits in the header. A deadline pill reads '4 days left'. Filed proposal: text-field validation 'plausibility-against-history'.
